page.layout: One page of running text in one column, with a running head and page number at the top. Below the head, a full-width italic line continues the previous page's paragraph. Then the heading "Probatio." and the main text. At the foot: signature "Ff 4" and catchword "in" at the right. No marginal notes.

p.i: quemadmodum & de lege præter alios testatur Dauid, & de Euangelio Apostolus.

main_text.p: Hæ Theses de perspicuitate scripturæ propter Pontificios confirmandæ sunt: qui scripturam in fundamento salutis accusant obscuritatis, ut suas etiam præstigias & Sera-phicas glossas cum scriptura necessario re-cipienda esle obtineant. Quanta uero cum contumelia Spiritus sancti id faciant, qui ubique in uerbo suo nobiscum quasi balbu-tit, & ad ruditatem nostram se demittit: nulli qui Scripturam sanctam unquam recte legit, obscurum esle potest. Dauid Psal.119. Legem Dei uocat lucernam pedum nostrorum, & lumen semitarum nostrarum, lucem quæ in-telligentiam paruulis conferat. Salomon Prouerb.1. testatur, se scribere ad dandam simplicibus solertiam, pueris scientiam & prudentiam: sapientiam foris clamare, & in plateis edere uocem suam: Paulus 1.Cor.1.& 2.dicit, se à Christo missum esle ad prædican-dum Euangelium, non cum sermonis peri-tia, neque cum eminentia facundiæ aut per-suasoriis humanæ sapientiæ verbis, ne ina-nis reddatur crux Christi: Et alibi 2.Cor.4. Euangelium uocat lumen gloriæ Christi. Petrus Propheticum sermonem, qui tamen non parum obscuritatis habere uidetur, lu-cernam uocat lucentem in caliginoso loco. page.notes: Running head is "SCRIPTURA." with page number 455 at the top right. The signature "Ff 4" at the foot is read from a tilted, small print and may be partly unclear. Printed long s (s) is written as s throughout, and u/v is normalised by vowel/consonant value (e.g. uero, uerbo, uocat, uidetur, uel). The printed forms "esle" and "Psal." are kept as printed, with long s rendered as plain s. The left margin shows only the edge of the neighbouring page and show-through, which are not transcribed.
